question: Which earlier works does this field build on, and in which schools?

frandsen2017.cite: Frandsen (2017). Evolution of modularity literature: a 25-year bibliometric analysis. International Journal of Operations & Production Management.
frandsen2017.checked: every quote read word for word in the vault's copy of the accepted author manuscript (library No. 227) on 20 Nov 2026; places are given as the manuscript's sections, since its page numbers differ from the journal's; the defining paper, Small (1973), is behind a paywall and was not read

steps.title: Collect citations
steps.text: Gather a field's papers and their reference lists: which later paper cites which earlier work.

steps.title: Count pairs
steps.text: For every pair of earlier works, count how many later papers cite both. That count is their co-citation strength.

quotes.text: co-citation, which measures the number of vertices that point toward both vertices i and j.
In citation analysis, two articles that are similar to other articles typically cite both

steps.title: Cluster
steps.text: Link works by their co-citation strength and look for groups: works often cited together pull into a cluster.

quotes.text: a high number of co-occurrences among cited references indicates proximity in the ideas of the articles.

steps.title: Read the base
steps.text: Read the works in each cluster to name the idea they share. Together the clusters map the field's intellectual base.

quotes.text: Kauffman (1993) and Levinthal (1997) are related as an element in the intellectual structure underpinning the modularity literature.

steps.title: Mind the lag
steps.text: A work joins the map only once later papers cite it, so this year's papers are invisible. Bibliographic coupling sees them at once.

quotes.text: A benefit of bibliometric coupling analysis is, that it allows for the inclusion of recent articles.

exercise.title: Count the links yourself
exercise.intro: Four older works (top) are cited by four later papers (bottom). Pick two works and count how many papers cite both: that is co-citation. Switch to coupling to count the references two papers share. Then publish a paper today and look for it on both maps.
